focus: Connector registry design: the smallest way for skilled bots to name a bot's apps, grant them per bot and record each use, on top of MCP and Code Mode, without building an OAuth server
noveltyJustification: 6 of 10 findings are new code facts (the 14-server UTCP config, the single dotenv secret path, the one-launcher MCP surface, the pass-through launcher, the existing environment allowlist, the closed frontmatter key set) and 4 restate prior evidence as design constraints; a 0.10 simplicity bonus applies because the design collapses to one frontmatter key, one filtered config write and one record field.
ruledOut: building an OAuth server (the largest piece of OpenBot's app layer and the one a small team can skip)
per-person connections (they need a sign-in surface and a session store)
a connector catalogue (the UTCP config already names the servers this team has)
